last_debrief: STORY SO FAR: Tue 11-10 morning, chat only, page only, his request ('best lesson you can muster'). November arc opened: Andrew's first night in the upstairs room, everyone speaks TO him. GIVE: the tail rhymes with its person (neenga -eenga, avan -aan, avanga -aanga, naan -en, nee -a/-iya) and the odd one, -om, with naama (we, you too) vs naanga (we, not you). MAP shown (Nov wk 2). SCENE, one ask per beat: Karthi 'Naanga saaptom. Nee saaptiya?' -> NEE RIGHT (was read as 'we' twice on 10-30), naanga read as THEY again; peg given: naan inside naanga, avan inside avanga. Paati 'Saapteengala?' -> first he translated it, then with both options shown fired 'ama sappiten' (hinted). Deepa 'Naama terrace-ku polaam' -> 'we went to the terrace': we RIGHT and himself included, polaam read as past; taught polaam vs ponom. HE VOLUNTEERED namma = our (namma ooru) and tested it against naama - right; given namma/enga as the our-pair. Priya 'Neengalum poneengala?' with pon- + your tail -> 'ama ponam ?' (ponom or ponen unclear; no credit; both given). Mama 'Room nalla irukkaa?' -> 'room nalla iruken': put his new -en on an it; after the recast he opened his next message with 'room nalla irukku' unprompted. Paati 'Idhu namma veedu. Seriya?' -> read whole line right. CARRY: he answered every addressed turn, six of six, short and fast; misses did not flatten him this time (one ask per beat, meaning given first). Endings still read loosely: naanga=they, -laam=done. Soak ordered: the rhyme by ear, lines said to him. Still unheard: M97, M98. Receptive check never run by ear. vaanginom still untaught. NEXT: a different room (errand with Karthi or homework with Deepa), -om vs -aanga by EAR, and Mama via the children. Hook: which 'our' does Mama use about the upstairs room?

soak_order.focus: What the 11-10 session taught, by ear: the tail rhymes with its person (naan -en, nee -a/-iya, avan -aan, avanga -aanga, neenga -eenga) and naanga/naama -om; naama (we, you too) against naanga (we, not you); polaam (let's go) against ponom (we went); irukku for a thing against irukken for me. Two stems throughout: saapidu, po.
